description: Build 91 can only claim a build-90 StoreKit purchase after the user upgrades and uploads signed proof. It cannot protect an immutable build-90 client that was charged but never upgrades. Releasing therefore requires ONE external fact this repo cannot itself prove: (a) provider/TestFlight evidence that build 90 can no longer initiate checkout, or (b) an owner-approved, explicitly bounded charged-before-upgrade recovery policy. This artifact is evaluated by apps/ios/Scripts/build90_recovery_gate.py, which is wired into verify_build91_entitlement_contract.py and FAILS CLOSED until one evidence form is supplied and complete. Do not fabricate evidence.

resolution.basis: Owner attestation by Dov Ginsburg, recorded 2026-07-25T03:22:28Z: no one has paid for Tono yet through Stripe, App Store, or Google Play. Therefore no charged build-90 user exists and no historical entitlement restoration is required.
resolution.scope_note: The recovery policy below is a safety net over an owner-attested EMPTY population, not a make-good for known affected users. If the attestation is ever contradicted by a provider report showing a build-90 charge, re-open this gate and treat the policy as live.
not_claimed: checkout_disabled evidence is NOT supplied: no App Store Connect observation of build 90 was performed. ASC private keys exist on the release machine but no issuer id is available, so a read-only ASC query was not possible.
No provider report (Stripe, App Store Connect, Play Console) was queried to corroborate the attestation; the no-payment fact rests on the owner's attestation.

notes: Operators may supply real evidence out-of-band via the TONO_BUILD90_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE env var (path to a JSON file with the same 'evidence' object) instead of committing it here.
The two evidence forms are mutually sufficient: exactly one complete form flips the gate to READY.

bounded_window_days = 90 was NOT stated by the owner. The gate requires a positive integer, and the owner attested the affected population is empty, so 90 days is recorded as a conservative safety-net window. Change it freely; it binds no known user.
